question: The daemon's reclamation tick fired 412 times in five hours and 81 MiB is still sitting free inside the allocator. Why does a trim that runs return nothing, and is the tick measuring the wrong thing or asking the wrong allocator?
why_now: Found by bounded-memory-long-session.json on 2026-09-14, which set out to state a bound and found that it could not say which half of the number belongs to the service and which to glibc. A daemon resting at 129 MiB of which 78 is allocator-held is not the same claim as one resting at 129 MiB, and a bound that does not distinguish them is the coin flip this project has already objected to once.

what_is_known.capped_and_busy: Fedora, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1, after re-indexing 184,000 items: RSS 129 MiB, 412 trims, free_arena 81.2 MiB, retained 77.9 MiB. Plateaued -- the second half of a five-hour run subtracted 3.7 MiB.
what_is_known.uncapped_and_idle: Ubuntu, no cap, a day of a listing a minute and no indexing: RSS 42 MiB, 0 trims, free_arena 25.3 MiB, retained 27.2 MiB. It never had a high-water mark to return.
what_is_known.what_capping_did_do: Removed the variance: 0.7 MiB of spread across six concurrent read workloads against 55.1 uncapped. That was measured before the shipped unit was changed and stands.

hypotheses.H1: malloc_trim returns only what is at the top of the heap, and the free space is fragmented below a live allocation, so there is nothing contiguous to give back. Distinguishable by looking at where the free space sits rather than how much there is.
hypotheses.H2: The pages are returned and taken again immediately, so RSS never falls -- 412 trims in 300 minutes is more than one a minute, which is a suspicious cadence for something that is supposed to fire on a threshold.
hypotheses.H3: The tick reads a figure that is not the one it can act on, so it fires on a number that trimming cannot move. daemon-allocator-arenas.json warned about exactly this shape once before: a trigger that could not fire went unnoticed until a measurement went looking.

how: Not decided yet. It needs the allocator's own accounting rather than RSS, and a run that indexes deliberately rather than by accident.
verdict: WITHDRAWN. Registered on a misreading of a designed cadence as a malfunction; see withdrawn above.

withdrawn.when: 2026-09-14, within the hour it was registered
withdrawn.why: The premise was wrong. 412 trims in five hours, and 708 on the development machine over twelve, is not a tick firing on a figure it cannot act on -- it is the cadence, once a minute, working exactly as designed. The reclamation trigger was deliberately changed from a threshold to a cadence precisely because free arena bytes and resident-minus-live do not fall when a trim succeeds and so fire forever; all three threshold attempts are recorded as failures in trim-cadence.json. free_arena_bytes exceeding RSS is likewise a known property of mallinfo2's fordblks, which counts free space in the heap and not resident pages, and is exactly why it is not the trigger.
withdrawn.what_I_should_have_done: Read trim-cadence.json before writing three hypotheses about a mechanism it already explains. The comment above the trigger says all of this in the source.
withdrawn.what_survives: Nothing as a defect. The five-hour series does answer a question that was genuinely open, and it is recorded in trim-cadence.json where it belongs rather than here.
